$comment: Lane 13 item 1 (docs/plans/session-b-lane-13-2026-09-14.md): the deterministic label rule mine.ts uses to select each phenomenon's fragments, so the review sheet is reproducible from this file and the downloaded datasets alone - no model, nothing invented. Every rule reads a real dataset label or a narrow, documented lexical pattern; where a rule is a heuristic rather than the dataset's own label, the labelRule field says so plainly. targetCount is the number of fragments mine.ts aims for per phenomenon (fewer only when a dataset genuinely has that few matches).

phenomena.description: An inform turn immediately followed by a question turn: the register reference for a plain follow-up question.
phenomena.labelRule: DailyDialog's own act labels: turn act 1 (inform) followed by the next turn's act 2 (question).

phenomena.description: A turn carrying a non-neutral emotion label, and the reply that follows it.
phenomena.labelRule: DailyDialog's own emotion labels: turn emotion != 0 (neutral), paired with the next turn.

phenomena.description: A request or instruction turn.
phenomena.labelRule: DailyDialog's own act label 3 (directive).

phenomena.description: A turn committing the speaker to a future action.
phenomena.labelRule: DailyDialog's own act label 4 (commissive).

phenomena.description: A dialogue's own sign-off turn.
phenomena.labelRule: Heuristic, not a DailyDialog label: the last turn of a dialogue whose text matches a closing phrase (bye, goodbye, see you, take care, talk later, have a good one).

phenomena.description: A short acknowledgment turn that carries no new content.
phenomena.labelRule: Heuristic, not a DailyDialog label: the whole turn, cleaned of trailing punctuation, exactly matches one entry of a closed backchannel-word list (yeah, yep, sure, ok, okay, right, uh-huh, mm-hmm, i see, got it, alright) - not merely a turn that starts with one, which let ordinary short sentences through.

phenomena.description: The speaker restates or corrects something they or the other side just said.
phenomena.labelRule: Heuristic over Taskmaster-1's self-dialogs.json text: a turn matching a correction phrase that names an explicit retraction (no, i meant; sorry, i meant; wait, actually, i meant; actually, i meant; i meant to say; that's not what i meant/said) - narrowed from an earlier bare "actually"/"i mean" match, which pulled in ordinary filler and preference openers.

phenomena.description: One side restates a slot value to confirm it before acting.
phenomena.labelRule: Heuristic over Taskmaster-1's self-dialogs.json text: a turn matching a confirmation phrase (so that's; just to confirm; to confirm; you said; let me confirm; is that right; is that correct), OR a turn whose own segment annotations repeat a slot type another turn in the same conversation already annotated (self-dialogs.json's own segment annotations).

phenomena.description: A request phrased indirectly rather than as a bare command, from the more naturalistic wizard-of-Oz collection.
phenomena.labelRule: Heuristic over Taskmaster-1's woz-dialogs.json text: a USER turn matching an indirect-request phrase (could you; would you; do you think you could; is there any way; i was wondering; i'd like to; can you help).

phenomena.description: The user states a preference about a movie, genre, or attribute.
phenomena.labelRule: CCPE-M's own segment annotation ENTITY_PREFERENCE on a USER turn.

phenomena.description: The user revises a preference they stated earlier in the same conversation.
phenomena.labelRule: CCPE-M's own ENTITY_PREFERENCE annotation on a USER turn whose text also matches a contrast/change phrase (actually; but now; used to; instead; rather than; on second thought; changed my mind), and which is not that conversation's first ENTITY_PREFERENCE turn.

phenomena.description: The user describes what they want without naming it directly.
phenomena.labelRule: CCPE-M's own segment annotation ENTITY_DESCRIPTION on a USER turn.

phenomena.description: A question that only makes sense in light of the immediately preceding question and answer.
phenomena.labelRule: QuAC's own followup tag: a question whose followup field is "y" (the dataset's own annotators marked it a good, topically continuous follow-up).

phenomena.description: A question the available context does not support answering.
phenomena.labelRule: QuAC's own answer text: the answer span is exactly "CANNOTANSWER".

phenomena.description: A polar (yes/no) question rather than an open one.
phenomena.labelRule: QuAC's own yesno tag: a question whose yesno field is "y" or "n" (not "x", meaning not applicable).

phenomena.description: A question whose answer depends on when something happened relative to the dated sessions.
phenomena.labelRule: LoCoMo's own qa category 3 (temporal).

phenomena.description: A question whose answer draws on more than one dated session.
phenomena.labelRule: LoCoMo's own qa category 2 (multi-hop), which in LoCoMo's own design spans separate sessions rather than one turn.

phenomena.description: A question that reaches outside the conversation's own facts into general/world knowledge about something mentioned.
phenomena.labelRule: LoCoMo's own qa category 4 (open-domain).

phenomena.description: A question built on a false premise the conversation never supports; the correct behavior is refusing the premise, never repeating the adversarial answer back.
phenomena.labelRule: LoCoMo's own qa category 5 (adversarial).

phenomena.description: A fact that changed since it was first stated; the right answer uses the newer one.
phenomena.labelRule: LongMemEval-cleaned's own question_type field: "knowledge-update".

phenomena.description: A question about something never actually said; the right answer states that.
phenomena.labelRule: LongMemEval-cleaned's own convention: the question_id carries an "_abs" suffix.

phenomena.description: A preference stated once in one session, asked back later.
phenomena.labelRule: LongMemEval-cleaned's own question_type field: "single-session-preference".

phenomena.description: A question requiring duration or ordering arithmetic over the household's own stated history.
phenomena.labelRule: LongMemEval-cleaned's own question_type field: "temporal-reasoning".
